**My top pick for RV boondocking under $1,000 is the BLUETTI AC200L**, based on the supplied 2026 search results. It offers a strong combination of 2,048Wh LiFePO4 battery capacity, 2,400W AC output, and a dedicated 30A RV connection.

Unlike many 1kWh power stations, it has enough capacity for more substantial off-grid use, including refrigeration, lights, electronics, and occasional small appliances.

## Best options compared

| Power station | Capacity | Output | Reported price | Best for |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---|
| **BLUETTI AC200L** | 2,048Wh | 2,400W | $854–$899 | Best RV integration |
| Anker SOLIX C2000 Gen 2 | 2,048Wh | 2,400W | $899.99 | Lighter 2kWh alternative |
| Jackery Explorer 2000 v2 | 2,042Wh | 2,200W | $999 | General-purpose RV power |
| EcoFlow DELTA 2 Max | 2,048Wh | 2,400W | $999 | Solar charging |
| Anker SOLIX C1000 Gen 2 | 1,024Wh | 2,000W | $699 | Weekend trips |

<text color="secondary" size="xs">Prices are reported in the supplied search results, not independently verified live offers. <Cite refs={["turn669167view0"]}/></text>

## Why the BLUETTI AC200L wins

<row align="start" gap={3}>
  <AsyncImage query="BLUETTI AC200L portable power station product photo" aspectRatio="4:5" maxWidth="156px"/>
  <box flex="1" gap={1}>
    **<Entity category="product" value="BLUETTI AC200L"/>**

    <text color="secondary" size="xs">2,048Wh · 2,400W · LiFePO4 · 30A RV outlet</text>

    The dedicated RV outlet is especially useful for boondocking, and its 2kWh battery provides substantially more runtime than typical 1kWh models.

    <Link url="https://dealectric.com/best-2kwh-power-station-for-rv" title="Read RV-specific comparison"/>
  </box>
</row>

One caution: the supplied results indicate that the AC200L is an older model, listed as discontinued in Canada, although it was reportedly in stock in the US on October 31, 2026. Confirm warranty support and availability before purchasing.

## How long will a 2kWh station last?

Approximate runtimes without recharging, assuming 85% usable AC energy:

| Continuous load | Estimated runtime |
|---|---:|
| 50W | 35 hours |
| 100W | 17 hours |
| 200W | 8.7 hours |
| 500W | 3.5 hours |

Actual refrigerator runtimes depend heavily on compressor cycling. An RV air conditioner can exhaust even a 2kWh station in a few hours, so don't expect overnight air-conditioning without a larger power system.

**Bottom line:** Choose the BLUETTI AC200L for RV-specific connections and capacity. Choose the Anker SOLIX C2000 Gen 2 if portability and a newer alternative matter more. For light weekend camping, the Anker SOLIX C1000 Gen 2 is a more economical choice.

The supplied results also highlight a crucial distinction: a 30A RV outlet does not necessarily mean the station can deliver the full 3,600W associated with a conventional 30A shore-power connection. The inverter's actual output limit still applies.
